One field (table_caption_bold) is a deliberately open, unresolved question -- see its entry below -- not silently omitted.

source.note: 22/22 zero exceptions -- no terminal period, no punctuation after the number label. JCSHM's own author-facing submission guidelines do not state a table-caption punctuation rule (only a figure one), so this is corroboration-by-sampling rather than a guideline-page citation.

source.quote: this session's own pre-submission QA sweep catching 2/37 real table captions in this project's own manuscript+SI with a stray trailing period that the other 35 did not carry
source.note: The QA-sweep finding is a real-document consistency check, not itself the source of the rule -- the rule comes from the 22-caption external sample; the QA catch is corroborating evidence that JCSHM's own norm (no trailing period) was violated by 2 outliers.

source.citation: genuinely unresolved -- not merely 'not yet researched'
source.note: Real published JCSHM articles bold the ENTIRE table caption (label + description), a DIFFERENT convention from figures (label-only bold, see figure_caption_bold above), but JCSHM's own author-facing submission guidelines never state a table-caption bold rule the way they explicitly do for figures. Whether 'bold the whole caption' is an author-submission-time requirement or a copyediting-stage transformation applied after acceptance is genuinely unknown from anything sourced this session. Even if resolved, audit_caption_style's caption_label_not_bold check only examines the LABEL run(s), not the full caption text, so a real 'bold the whole caption' rule would need a second, differently-scoped check too, not just this value. Do not guess a value here -- this field intentionally stays value:null/tier:4 until a future pass resolves both the sourcing gap and the detection-scope gap together.

source.note: 2026-09-17 correction from an earlier stale 240 -- the original PDF-baseline line-count measurement could not cleanly separate a heading's own after-spacing from the following paragraph's before-spacing under rendered spacing collapse. Two independent, non-rendering sources (the real LaTeX class file AND a live article's own CSS) converge exactly on 6pt=120 twips, re-verified live in this session rather than re-read from a prior report. Both real submission documents already in production (staging/jcshm_v58_section2_refs_indent_ooxml_safe_20260904, review44/review63 candidates, 107 headings) already carry 120 twips -- the preset default was the stale artifact, not the documents.
